scientific_reframe: Under what combinations of nanosystem design, biological transport, trigger specificity, payload release, immune compatibility, clearance, and manufacturing control can an injectable nanosystem improve disease-site therapy over non-robotic carriers or free drug?
author_requirements: distinguish nanocarriers, nanomachines, nanorobots, and microrobots
anchor the animal evidence in the 2018 DNA nanorobot tumor study
derive low-Reynolds transport and target-to-off-target indices
include human flow, blood compatibility, staged animal, and translation gates
separate trigger-gated therapeutic function from general autonomous robotics
report no observed results because the workflow is design-only
include immune, toxicity, manufacturing, regulatory, and safety boundaries
